locator.section: 8.x Bond lability / heterolytic vs homolytic dissociation at an EE+ site

evidence.curator_note: adduct corrected to null: the precursor is an even-electron oxonium ion (charge +1, radical_electrons 0), not the [M]+. molecular ion. Equation 8.18, bottom row labelled 'homolytic' (bond marked 'strong'): the same generic even-electron oxonium ion R'(O+H)-R dissociates homolytically to give the alcohol radical cation R'OH+. and the neutral alkyl radical .R. Book draws 2 arc(s); moves <1,2> are BOTH drawn -- two single-barbed fishhooks that split the O-R bonding pair, one electron staying on oxygen (giving the O+. radical cation) and one going to the departing R (giving .R). No implicit hook is required: the two fishhooks fully produce the two odd-electron products. GENERIC scheme: R'=CH3 and R=C2H5 are a curator-chosen instantiation (protonated methyl ethyl ether, C3H9O+); the book prints no specific structures, m/z, or intensities. Text: 'homolytic bond cleavage forms two odd-electron products, and so usually requires much more energy' -- the higher-energy ('strong' bond) path, disfavoured relative to the heterolytic route (Eq. 8.18a) but discussed as important for reactions such as RY+-H -> RY+. + .H (Eq. 8.19).
